doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: Backing tracks, laptops and the Linn drum machine
summary: Rick on computers replacing live bands at Turning Stone; Zito's brief try with a Linn machine.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: So now Frankie Valli comes in like at the Turning Stone Casino where I used to do contracting for all the acts that came in.
But nobody’s left. And at some point everybody would come in with the computer.

All right? So all the tracks, everything is on the computer. They play but at some point you know like Frankie Vallee and some of those high parts, they just push up his track and that was that. And virtually every act that came through turned in that direction.
Where was this, where was this now?
At Turning Stone Casino up here.

So for years contracting those acts they would come in and play, like Aretha Franklin and like that, and little by little you’d see the computer. The drummer would have the laptop and he’d be pushing up tracks with the headphones.

You know man I bought a Linn drum machine when they first came out many years ago, because people were asking me if I programmed. Right? Do you have a machine? Could you — do you have a machine? And I’d say — so I went out and bought one you know, it was like 28 hundred dollars or something. Fantastic sounds in Linn drum machine, the old Linn. I still have it. But I would go to a date and play, and then I’d take the drum part and go home, get the machine out and try to program what I played. You know? And I did it for about two weeks and I just put it away one day man. I said I still want to play. I’m still learning how to play the drums. What am I learning now pressing buttons? It had nothing to do with our make-up as a person. And I put it away man, and then it took over. The guys that were doing dates man, you know there were a couple of mediocre drummers that bought drum machines man that made a lot of money man. And they programmed well, they did. They knew what they were doing. I’m terrible with technology man, as you know.
